recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-16958 unless the work group separately wants a non-semantic editorial typo cleanup of the existing word "processer".
issue_request: FHIR-16958 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes change request asking whether Identifier.value could be made unconditionally case sensitive; the accepted resolution says Identifier.system is always case sensitive, while Identifier.value is treated as case sensitive unless knowledge of Identifier.system makes non-case-sensitive processing safe.
initial_application: The Jira comment records application in SVN revision 14160. Git commit a5c90c3db3cc87902faf8b096c1fdc5f179853fc on 2018-07-29, with subject "GF#16131, GF#16940, GF#16958, GF#16959, GF#16966: documentation improvements on data types, + precision extension", added the requested Identifier.system and Identifier.value wording to source/datatypes.html and source/datatypes/identifier.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Identifier in the active [types] section, so the datatype narrative and spreadsheet are in current build scope. Bounded Jira/Zulip/Confluence searches found no final core reversal or conflicting community record; a broad Jira search also returned a Triaged US Identity Matching issue that is outside this core reconciliation scope.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current datatype narrative says Identifier.system is always case sensitive and Identifier.value is treated as case sensitive unless Identifier.system knowledge allows safe non-case-sensitive processing; the Identifier.system and Identifier.value spreadsheet rows also carry the same rule.

related_jiras.note: The historical application commit bundled GF#16959 with GF#16958; FHIR-16959 already has a separate combined-branch audit commit and was not republished here.
